samples.claim: Timestamp encoding is timestamp:unit:timezone; absent timezone uses -, present timezone text is verbatim. Duration uses duration:unit; Struct uses struct. Dictionary first converts value and index types, constructs dict:value:index:false, then immediately parses the result back through DataType::try_from. Failure becomes Error::schema explaining the type/string does not parse back, preventing a later Field::data_type unwrap on strings that embed unrepresentable colon-separated components or child-dependent types. The check is parse success, not exact Arrow identity (views normalize). List/LargeList distinguish a Struct element with .struct suffix; they do not inline the child logical type.

samples.claim: project(path) clones all parent properties into a field with no children. Empty path restores all original children; a matching next child recursively projects only it. Missing next child returns Ok with empty children, rather than a missing-field error, which can later produce an invalid nested field. No atomic map/blob handling appears here. project_by_filter evaluates descendants first and retains a field if any child survives or its predicate returns true. The predicate is short-circuited for a parent with retained children. The documentation's nonmatch=>None shorthand omits this ancestor-retention rule.
samples.review_notes: Confirmed implementation. Clarify that the final Returns None sentence is incomplete while preceding doc lines729-730 explicitly describe ancestor retention. Add data_type citation for later panic risk.
